newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mannesmann says Omnitel deal is off. [CORRECTED 09:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Mannesmann says Omnitel deal is off. [CORRECTED 09:50 GMT]

text.p: German engineering and telecommunications group Mannesmann AG said on Tuesday it would no longer carry out a planned acquisition of additional shares in Italy's Omnitel mobile phone group.

Mannesmann said in a statement that Bell Atlantic (corrects company name from "BellSouth") of the United States had exercised first purchase rights to 8.26 percent stake in Omnitel Sistemi Radiocellulari (OSR) from Olivetti that it believed it had clinched last month.
The deal would have indirectly raised Mannesmann's stake in Omnitel Pronto Italia, Italy's second mobile phone group, by 5.8 percent because the Omnitel consortium holds 70 percent of OSR.

Olivetti is Omnitel's biggest shareholder. Bell will buy the 8.26 percent stake in OSR -- or a 5.8 percent indirect stake in Omnitel -- on the same terms as Mannesmann had agreed, that is to pay 432.5 billion lire ($283 million).

Last month, Mannesmann which was already a shareholder in Omnitel signed a contract to buy the 8.26 percent stake from Olivetti, but as required by the by-laws of OSR, the sale was subject to pre-emptive rights of the other shareholders.

These shareholders which included Swedish state-owned telecoms operator Telia, U.S. Cellular Communications International Inc (CCIL), as well as Bell and Olivetti, had thirty days to exercise their rights on the same terms as stipulated in the Mannesmann contract which was to be activated in early to mid November.

Bell, which already had a 16.9 percent stake in OSR, was exercising its right to buy the stake bringing its total up to 24.9 percent, while other OSR partners CCIL and Telia had not exercised their rights.
